llm.summary: This planning skill is mostly transparent, but it tells the agent to automatically move from planning into execution without asking the user first.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is project planning, but the artifact requires auto-invoking `attune:project-execution` after saving `docs/implementation-plan.md`, which can move beyond planning into implementation actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow continuation is disclosed, but it explicitly says not to prompt for confirmation; the only user-control bypass is if the user already asked to stop or used `--standalone`.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only a markdown skill file, with no executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, or obfuscated content found in the supplied artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Creating an implementation plan under `docs/implementation-plan.md` is proportionate for a planning skill, but automatically handing off to an execution skill is broader than the planning phase normally implies.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background persistence, credential access, or privilege escalation is present, but the skill does direct creation of a persistent project document and an automatic transition to a potentially mutating next phase.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the planning workflow automatically continuing into execution. To keep it planning-only, use the documented `--standalone` flag or explicitly tell the agent to stop after producing the plan.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] unexpected: The cited behavior is present in `SKILL.md`: after quality checks it must auto-invoke `Skill(attune:project-execution)` and must not ask for confirmation. This supports a Review verdict because execution can exceed a user’s expectation for a planning-only skill, even though the behavior is openly documented and not malicious.
